title: The Unamended Code
question: Has novelty's stated definition changed over nine years, the way its enforcement has?

figures.title: Distance of each year's sentences to the 2026 code
figures.deck: 2018's reasoning fits the 2026 rulebook almost as well as 2026's own held-out half does — 0.159 against a 0.152 calibration.

claims.statement: 2018's reasoning fits the 2026 rulebook almost as well as 2026's own held-out half does — 0.159 against a 0.152 calibration.
claims.derivation: 2018's mean embedding distance to the 2026 code (dist_to_2026["2018"] = 0.159) compared to the code's own held-out-half calibration distance (control.heldout_2026 = 0.1516 → 0.152)

claims.statement: Stated with its uncertainty: the earliest years do sit measurably above it (2018–20 run about +0.006, two to three bootstrap standard errors — and sentences cluster within reviews, so even that overstates the certainty).
claims.derivation: dist_to_2026[year] − control.heldout_2026, for 2018–2020, averaging about +0.006, against dist_se giving a two-to-three-SE gap

claims.statement: Every year 2018–2026 sits within 0.008 of that line, so the null is a claim about size, not undetectability.
claims.derivation: max over all nine years of dist_to_2026[year] − control.heldout_2026

figures.title: The clause mix, year by year
figures.deck: The same six clauses in every year — with one slow tilt: differentiation slips 50% → 38% while combination absorbs it.

claims.statement: One slow tilt is real: the differentiation clause's share slips from 50% in 2018 to 38% in 2026, with the combination clause absorbing most of it.
claims.derivation: mix_by_year["2018"].diff = 0.50 to mix_by_year["2026"].diff = 0.381, ≈38%; mix_by_year["2018"].combination = 0.2987 to mix_by_year["2026"].combination = 0.3428 absorbs most of the drop

claims.statement: All six clauses are present in every year of the record — the differentiation clause holds 36–50%, the combination clause 29–35%, the transfer clause 5–7%.
claims.derivation: min/max across all nine years of mix_by_year[year].diff, .combination, .transfer

caveats.text: An embedding distance can only see changes large enough to shift the phrasing, and the six clauses are coarse; sentence embeddings could miss a subtle semantic shift that preserves register.
The null is a claim about size, not undetectability — a drift of a few percent in the rule's phrasing, beside the double-digit relative swings in its enforcement one plate back (Plate XXVI).

The transfer clause rides on the code's one genuinely mixed cluster — most of its sentences describe applying a known technique in a new setting, though some read equally well as ordinary differentiation claims — so its band is the least certain of the six.
